financials_interim.notes: Source: Aitken Spence PLC (SPEN) Interim Statements for the Three Months Ended 30 June 2026 (subject to audit, board-approved 13 Aug 2026), downloaded from CSE cdn (source_id 52595). This is the FIRST financial_statements row for SPEN in this DB -- the only prior local document was for the quarter/year ended 31 March 2025 (Q4 FY2024/25, manual_851f31c0a4767bb9), which is not a usable interim predecessor for this Q1 FY2026/27 quarter (different quarter, 15 months stale) -- YoY only, vs the filing's own 3-months-ended-30-June-2025 comparative column. SPEN has a 31 March financial year end (Q1 FY2026/27). Note: SPEN is the parent of AHUN (Aitken Spence Hotel Holdings PLC), which is being entered separately by a different process in this DB -- this entry does NOT touch AHUN's data; AHUN's results feed into SPEN's Tourism-sector segment and consolidated Group figures only as a component, not reproduced independently here. Separate GROUP and COMPANY columns given throughout -> entered as two rows per project convention. Figures in Rs'000 (unit_scale='000'). Income statement (both bases): p.2. Balance sheet (both bases): p.4. Cash flow statement (both bases): p.7-8. Segmental note (Tourism / Maritime and freight logistics / Strategic investments / Services sectors): p.9. Non-financial info (shares/shareholders): p.11. Mapping: SPEN uses a NATURE-OF-EXPENSE income statement format (raw materials, employee benefits, depreciation, other operating expenses direct/indirect), not a cost-of-sales/gross-profit format -- cost_of_sales and gross_profit are left NULL for both bases since no such subtotal is disclosed anywhere in the filing; this is a genuine format difference, not a missing figure. revenue = 'Revenue' as printed (before deduction of 'Revenue taxes' of 424,499 Group / 7,534 Company, which nets to 'Net revenue' 18,532,305 Group / 386,890 Company -- the gross 'Revenue' line is used as the revenue field to match this DB's convention of using the top disclosed revenue line; revenue taxes are not separately fielded). operating_profit = 'Profit from operations' (Group 2,048,122 vs 1,537,780 PY; Company 1,126,886 vs 656,917 PY). finance_income/finance_costs = 'Finance income' and 'Finance expenses' gross lines as separately disclosed (unlike ACL/CSLK, SPEN discloses a full gross split, not just a net line) -- Group finance income 502,731, finance costs 1,748,145; Company finance income 517,851, finance costs 631,382. profit_before_tax includes 'Share of profit of equity-accounted investees' (941,857 Group; nil Company, since equity-accounted investees sit at Group level only) added after net finance expense, per the filing's own layout -- not separately fielded. profit_after_tax = 'Profit for the period' TOTAL including the portion attributable to non-controlling interests (Group 1,044,844 = equity holders' 1,451,977 minus NCI's absorbed LOSS of 407,133; Company 1,008,880, no NCI at Company level). minority_interest field = -407,133 (Group only) -- stored as NEGATIVE because NCI absorbed a net LOSS this quarter (Tourism-sector NCI, largely AHUN and other part-owned hotel subsidiaries, ran deeply loss-making this quarter -- see driver note below), unlike a typical positive NCI profit share. trade_receivables = 'Trade and other receivables' only (Group 15,996,716; Company 10,747,403); excludes 'Other current assets' (Group 30,624,161; Company 22,397,287, a very large balance not itemised in this filing -- likely inter-company/investment-related current assets given Company's size -- flagged as a genuine disclosure gap, not separately fielded) and 'Current tax receivable'/'Deposits and prepayments'. current_assets field = the filing's own printed subtotal '75,784,302' (Group) / '37,755,696' (Company), which EXCLUDES 'Assets classified as held for sale' (857,481 Group; 72,237 Company) -- held-for-sale assets sit as a separate SOFP caption between current and total, per the filing's own presentation; total_assets (231,756,182 Group; 58,809,086 Company) correctly includes them, but the current_assets field does not, matching the filing's own subtotal, not a computed figure -- flagged so this isn't mistaken for a balancing error (231,756,182 = 155,114,399 non-current + 75,784,302 current + 857,481 held-for-sale, cross-check passed). short_term_borrowings = current 'Interest-bearing loans and borrowings' + 'Bank overdrafts and other short-term borrowings' combined (Group: 6,777,186 + 23,485,912 = 30,263,098; Company: 1,040,330 + 12,974,516 = 14,014,846), same convention as ACL and CSLK entries in this DB. long_term_borrowings = non-current 'Interest-bearing loans and borrowings' only (Group 36,988,242; Company 5,720,160), excludes 'Lease liabilities' (Group 23,067,862 non-current -- material, mostly hotel-property leases, not a loan). capex = 'Purchase of property, plant and equipment' from the cash flow statement only (Group 629,596; Company 8,061); excludes 'Purchase of intangible assets' (Group 38,205) and 'Purchase of biological assets' (Group 1,260) which are separately disclosed lines with no dedicated FINANCIAL_FIELDS slot -- a mapping simplification, not a missing disclosure. EPS basic/diluted 3.58 (Group) cross-checks to PAT-to-owners 1,451,977 / 405,996,045 shares = 3.576, matches printed 3.58; Company EPS 2.48 cross-checks to 1,008,880 / 405,996,045 = 2.485, matches printed 2.48 (no separate diluted EPS disclosed, treated as same as basic). PBT-tax-PAT identity holds for both bases (Group: 1,744,565 - 699,721 = 1,044,844; Company: 1,013,355 - 4,475 = 1,008,880). Shares in issue 405,996,045 per Note 1 (p.11), unchanged from 31 March 2026. KEY OBSERVATION (segmental, Note 1.1, p.9, not fabricated): the Tourism sector (hotels/leisure, includes AHUN and other part/wholly-owned hotel subsidiaries) swung to a PBT LOSS of Rs.(1,008,911)k this quarter from a smaller PBT LOSS of Rs.(221,766)k a year earlier -- a Rs.787,145k YoY deterioration, the single largest negative segment swing and the reason NCI absorbed a net loss this quarter. This was more than offset at Group level by the Maritime and freight logistics sector, whose segment PBT rose 58.2% YoY to Rs.1,655,261k (2025: Rs.1,046,512k, +Rs.608,749k) on external revenue growth of 27.5% (Rs.4,609,493k vs Rs.3,614,104k), and by the Strategic investments sector, which swung from a PBT LOSS of Rs.(97,174)k to a PBT PROFIT of Rs.646,108k (+Rs.743,282k swing), driven largely by 'Share of profit of equity-accounted investees' which nearly doubled Group-wide (Rs.941,857k vs Rs.540,347k PY, +74.3%). Group PBT overall grew 74.2% YoY to Rs.1,744,565k (2025: Rs.1,001,946k) because the Maritime and Strategic-investments gains (combined +Rs.1,352,031k) outweighed the Tourism-sector deterioration (-Rs.787,145k).

thesis.thesis_text: Aitken Spence PLC is one of Sri Lanka's largest diversified conglomerates, spanning Tourism (hotels/leisure, including majority-owned AHUN), Maritime and Freight Logistics, Strategic Investments (equity-accounted associate stakes), and Services. In Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), Group PBT grew 74.2% YoY to Rs.1,744,565k and PAT grew 157.7% to Rs.1,044,844k despite essentially flat Group revenue (-1.2%) -- entirely a segment-mix outcome (Note 1.1, p.9): the Maritime and Freight Logistics segment delivered genuine, operationally-driven growth (PBT +58.2% on 27.5% external revenue growth), and the Strategic Investments segment swung to profit largely on rising equity-accounted associate income, together more than offsetting a Rs.787,145k deterioration in the Tourism segment's PBT loss -- a segment that includes SPEN's hotel subsidiary AHUN, itself reporting widening losses this quarter. At ~9.85x annualised P/E and ~0.54x P/B with a steady ~2.84% dividend yield, the stock is statistically cheap, but the filing offers no qualitative explanation (no MD&A section) for the Tourism deterioration, and Group operating cash flow was a net use of Rs.(2,536,553)k this quarter -- a genuinely mixed picture behind the strong headline growth (Interim Financial Statements, source_doc_id 52595, p.2 and Note 1.1 p.9).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no CBSL/tourism-demand/global-freight data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Confidence is limited: this is SPEN's FIRST financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (only a 15-month-stale FY2024/25 annual predates it, not usable for QoQ), so only a single YoY comparison exists; the Tourism segment's large PBT deterioration and the Strategic Investments segment's associate-income surge are both unexplained by qualitative company commentary (no MD&A section in this filing), and a very large unitemised 'Other current assets' balance (Rs.30,624,161k) further caps confidence.

financial_quality.rationale: Q1 FY2026/27 (qtr ended 30 June 2026) Group PBT grew 74.2% YoY to Rs.1,744,565k and PAT grew 157.7% to Rs.1,044,844k, but this masks real balance-sheet and cash-flow strain: Group Cash Used in Operating Activities widened to Rs.(2,536,553)k from Rs.(1,158,100)k PY, and Net Finance Expense worsened 15.7% YoY to Rs.1,245,410k as Finance Expenses grew faster (+16.3% to Rs.1,748,145k) than Finance Income (+17.6% to Rs.502,731k). Total liabilities/equity of 1.18x (125,387,994/106,368,188) and a current ratio of 1.38x (75,784,302/54,746,206) are moderate for a diversified conglomerate carrying Rs.43,765,430k of combined interest-bearing debt (up from Rs.42,581,690k at 31 March 2026), not stretched but not conservative either. Non-Controlling Interests absorbed a net LOSS of Rs.(407,133)k this quarter (2025: NCI loss of Rs.(128,360)k) because Tourism-sector subsidiaries carry material minority ownership and that segment deteriorated sharply -- a genuine earnings-quality flag sitting alongside the strong headline PAT growth.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group Revenue was essentially flat YoY (-1.2% to Rs.18,956,804k), yet PBT grew 74.2% -- a pure segment-mix story per the Segment Analysis (Note 1.1, p.9). The Tourism sector (hotels/leisure, includes AHUN and other part-owned hotel subsidiaries) swung to a DEEPER PBT loss of Rs.(1,008,911)k from Rs.(221,766)k a year earlier (a Rs.787,145k YoY deterioration), the single largest negative driver. This was more than offset by the Maritime and Freight Logistics sector, whose PBT rose a genuine, operationally-driven 58.2% YoY to Rs.1,655,261k on 27.5% external revenue growth (Rs.4,609,493k vs Rs.3,614,104k) -- real operating momentum, not an accounting item -- and by the Strategic Investments sector, which swung from a Rs.(97,174)k PBT loss to a Rs.646,108k profit, driven largely by Share of Profit of Equity-Accounted Investees nearly doubling Group-wide (Rs.941,857k vs Rs.540,347k PY, +74.3%) -- a lower-quality, less-controllable driver than Maritime's organic growth, though not a one-off gain either. Group Profit from Operations (pre-associate-income) still rose 33.2% YoY to Rs.2,048,122k, indicating the Maritime/Logistics and Services strength genuinely outweighed the Tourism drag even before the associate-income boost.

valuation.rationale: At Rs.141.00 (2026-08-31), annualising Q1 Group EPS (Rs.3.58 x4 = Rs.14.32) implies a P/E of ~9.85x, and book value of ~Rs.262.00/share (Group total equity Rs.106,368,188k / 405,996,045 shares) implies a P/B of ~0.54x -- statistically cheap on both counts for a large, diversified conglomerate with genuine operating businesses (Maritime and Freight Logistics being the standout). Dividends have held steady at Rs.4.00 (FY2026, FY2025) after Rs.4.25 (FY2024), implying a ~2.84% trailing yield. The annualised P/E should be treated with some caution since this quarter's PAT was flattered by the Strategic Investments segment's associate-income swing and depressed by the Tourism segment's widening loss -- neither is likely to repeat mechanically at the same magnitude.
citations: dividends: FY2026 DPS 4.00, FY2025 DPS 4.00, FY2024 DPS 4.25

business_quality.rationale: Aitken Spence PLC (Capital Goods sector per coverage universe) is one of Sri Lanka's largest diversified conglomerates, spanning Tourism (hotels/leisure, including majority stake in AHUN), Maritime and Freight Logistics (a genuine market-leading franchise in Sri Lankan port/freight services), Strategic Investments (equity-accounted associate stakes), and a smaller Services segment. This diversification is a real strength -- the Maritime and Freight Logistics segment's 27.5% external revenue growth and 58.2% PBT growth this quarter demonstrate a durable, non-tourism earnings engine that is currently offsetting genuine weakness in the Tourism segment (AHUN and other part-owned hotel subsidiaries), which is SPEN's most cyclical and currently weakest business line.

governance_risk.rationale: No circulars/disclosures feed exists in this project to independently verify board or ownership changes. The four-segment structure is disclosed transparently (Note 1.1, p.9), a positive for disclosure quality, but the filing gives NO qualitative explanation anywhere (no MD&A/Financial Review section) for the Tourism segment's Rs.787,145k YoY PBT deterioration -- a genuine, currently unexplained filing-level gap on the single largest negative driver this quarter. A very large Rs.30,624,161k 'Other current assets' balance (Group) also sits on the balance sheet with no itemisation.

key_reasons: Q1 FY2026/27 Group PBT grew 74.2% YoY to Rs.1,744,565k and PAT grew 157.7% to Rs.1,044,844k despite essentially flat revenue (-1.2%) -- a segment-mix story: Maritime and Freight Logistics PBT +58.2% (Rs.1,655,261k, on genuine 27.5% external revenue growth) and Strategic Investments swinging from a loss to a Rs.646,108k profit (largely equity-accounted associate income nearly doubling) together more than offset a Rs.787,145k deterioration in the Tourism segment's PBT loss

Statistically cheap at ~9.85x annualised trailing P/E and ~0.54x P/B, with a steady Rs.4.00 dividend (~2.84% yield), though the annualised EPS is flattered by non-repeating associate income and depressed by the Tourism drag in the same quarter

Tourism segment (includes AHUN) swung to a deeper PBT loss of Rs.(1,008,911)k from Rs.(221,766)k a year earlier, driving Non-Controlling Interests into a net loss of Rs.(407,133)k for the first time in this comparison -- unexplained qualitatively anywhere in the filing (no MD&A section)
watch_factors: Tourism segment's Rs.787,145k YoY PBT deterioration is the number to watch next quarter -- no MD&A/Financial Review section exists in this filing to explain whether it reflects specific hotel properties, occupancy trends, one-off costs, or currency effects

Group Cash Used in Operating Activities widened to Rs.(2,536,553)k from Rs.(1,158,100)k PY, and Net Finance Expense rose 15.7% YoY to Rs.1,245,410k -- both genuine cash-flow and cost drags sitting underneath the strong headline PAT growth

Strategic Investments segment's turnaround depends heavily on Share of Profit of Equity-Accounted Investees (+74.3% YoY to Rs.941,857k) -- the underlying investee(s) driving this are not individually named in the filing, so its durability cannot be independently assessed

horizon_notes.6m: Next quarterly filing will show whether the Tourism segment's loss (driven substantially by AHUN and other part-owned hotel subsidiaries) stabilises or continues to widen, and whether Maritime and Freight Logistics sustains its 27.5% revenue growth pace.
horizon_notes.1y: If Maritime and Freight Logistics keeps compounding at a similar pace, it could structurally re-rate SPEN's earnings mix away from Tourism cyclicality -- worth tracking segment PBT contribution over a full year.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on whether Tourism-segment losses (concentrated in AHUN, SPEN's hotel subsidiary) stabilise, since NCI is now absorbing losses rather than profits from that segment for the first time in this comparison.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/industry data source in this project to assess a multi-year Sri Lankan tourism-demand or global freight/logistics cycle relevant to SPEN's two largest segments.

interim_updates.note_text: Aitken Spence PLC (SPEN) reported Group Revenue of Rs.18,956.80mn for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), down 1.2% YoY from Rs.19,190.29mn, but Group Profit Before Tax rose 74.2% YoY to Rs.1,744.57mn (2025: Rs.1,001.95mn) and Profit for the Period rose 157.7% YoY to Rs.1,044.84mn (2025: Rs.405.37mn) -- a result driven almost entirely by segment mix shift, per the Segment Analysis (Note 1.1, p.9), which splits SPEN into four sectors: Tourism, Maritime and Freight Logistics, Strategic Investments, and Services. The Tourism sector (hotels/leisure, including AHUN and other part-owned hotel subsidiaries) swung to a DEEPER PBT LOSS of Rs.(1,008.91)mn this quarter from a smaller loss of Rs.(221.77)mn a year earlier -- a Rs.787.15mn YoY deterioration -- despite Tourism external revenue falling only 10.2% YoY (Rs.11,568.26mn vs Rs.12,879.24mn), pointing to margin/cost pressure within the segment rather than a pure volume story; this loss also explains why Non-Controlling Interests absorbed a NET LOSS of Rs.(407.13)mn this quarter (2025: NCI loss of Rs.(128.36)mn), since Tourism-sector subsidiaries carry material minority ownership. This was more than offset by the Maritime and Freight Logistics sector, whose segment PBT rose 58.2% YoY to Rs.1,655.26mn (2025: Rs.1,046.51mn, +Rs.608.75mn) on external revenue growth of 27.5% (Rs.4,609.49mn vs Rs.3,614.10mn), and by the Strategic Investments sector, which swung from a PBT LOSS of Rs.(97.17)mn to a PBT PROFIT of Rs.646.11mn (+Rs.743.28mn swing) -- largely reflecting 'Share of profit of equity-accounted investees', which nearly doubled Group-wide to Rs.941.86mn from Rs.540.35mn PY (+74.3%). The smaller Services sector grew steadily, PBT +64.8% YoY to Rs.452.11mn (2025: Rs.274.37mn) on revenue +2.8% to Rs.471.13mn. Net of these offsetting segment moves, Group Profit from Operations still rose 33.2% YoY to Rs.2,048.12mn (2025: Rs.1,537.78mn) even before the equity-accounted-investee gain, indicating the Maritime/Logistics and Services strength outweighed Tourism's operating deterioration at the operating-profit line too, not just at PBT. Group Net Finance Expense widened 15.7% YoY to Rs.1,245.41mn (2025: Rs.1,076.18mn) as Finance Expenses grew faster (+16.3% to Rs.1,748.15mn) than Finance Income (+17.6% to Rs.502.73mn), a modest drag on the otherwise strong PBT growth. At the Company (parent, holding-company-only) level, revenue grew 4.2% YoY to Rs.394.42mn but Profit from Operations nearly doubled, +71.5% YoY to Rs.1,126.89mn (2025: Rs.656.92mn), driven by Other Operating Income (chiefly dividends from subsidiaries) rising 67.8% YoY to Rs.1,229.92mn (2025: Rs.733.09mn) -- since Company-level revenue is small, dividend income from subsidiaries, not core parent-company operations, is the dominant driver of the Company-level profit increase. Group Cash flow from Operating Activities remained a net use of cash, Rs.(2,536.55)mn (2025: Rs.(1,158.10)mn used, a larger outflow YoY), while Interest-Bearing Loans and Borrowings (current + non-current combined) stood at Rs.43,765.43mn at Group level, up from Rs.42,581.69mn at 31 March 2026.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is SPEN's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB -- the only prior local document (quarter/year ended 31 March 2025, Q4 FY2024/25) is 15 months stale and not a usable interim predecessor for this Q1 FY2026/27 quarter, so only YoY (vs the filing's own 3-months-ended-30-June-2025 comparative column) is computed. SPEN is the parent of AHUN (Aitken Spence Hotel Holdings PLC), entered separately in this DB by a different process -- this entry does not reproduce or override AHUN's own standalone figures; AHUN feeds into SPEN's Tourism-sector segment and Group consolidated figures only. Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) the Tourism segment's Rs.787.15mn YoY PBT deterioration is not explained qualitatively anywhere in this filing -- there is no MD&A/Financial Review section (confirmed absent, p.1-12 reviewed in full), only the bare segmental table, so whether the deterioration reflects specific hotel properties, occupancy/ADR trends, one-off costs, or currency effects cannot be determined from this document; (2) a very large 'Other current assets' balance (Group Rs.30,624.16mn; Company Rs.22,397.29mn) sits on the balance sheet with no itemisation or note reference -- not mapped into any FINANCIAL_FIELDS slot, a genuine disclosure gap given its size relative to total current assets; (3) the exact composition of Non-Controlling Interests by segment/subsidiary is not disclosed (only the Group-level total), so the extent to which AHUN specifically (versus other part-owned Tourism-sector entities) drove the Rs.(407.13)mn NCI loss cannot be isolated from this filing alone; (4) 'Share of profit of equity-accounted investees' nearly doubling to Rs.941.86mn is not broken down by underlying investee, so which specific associate/JV drove the Strategic Investments turnaround is not disclosed.
interim_updates.takeaway: SPEN's headline PBT and PAT growth (+74.2% and +157.7% YoY) occurred despite essentially flat Group revenue (-1.2%), and is entirely a segment-mix story: the Maritime and Freight Logistics segment (+Rs.608.75mn PBT) and the Strategic Investments segment turnaround (+Rs.743.28mn, largely equity-accounted investee income) together more than offset a Rs.787.15mn deterioration in the Tourism (hotels/leisure) segment's PBT loss. The Tourism deterioration is the number to watch heading into next quarter -- it drove Non-Controlling Interests into a net loss position for the first time in this comparison, and the filing gives no qualitative explanation for it (no MD&A section at all), so whether it reflects seasonality, one-off costs, or a genuine deterioration in the hotels business cannot be determined from this document alone. Group-level operating profit growth (+33.2%) was also solid before the equity-accounted-investee boost, suggesting the Maritime/Logistics and Services strength is a genuine, cash-flow-relevant improvement, not purely an accounting item.
operational_highlights: Group Revenue Rs.18,956.80mn, -1.2% YoY (2025: Rs.19,190.29mn); Profit from Operations Rs.2,048.12mn, +33.2% YoY; PBT Rs.1,744.57mn, +74.2% YoY; PAT Rs.1,044.84mn, +157.7% YoY; EPS Rs.3.58 (2025: Rs.1.31).

Tourism sector PBT loss widened to Rs.(1,008.91)mn from Rs.(221.77)mn PY (a Rs.787.15mn deterioration) on external revenue -10.2% YoY to Rs.11,568.26mn -- the largest negative segment driver, and the reason Non-Controlling Interests absorbed a net loss of Rs.(407.13)mn this quarter.
Maritime and Freight Logistics segment PBT +58.2% YoY to Rs.1,655.26mn (2025: Rs.1,046.51mn) on external revenue +27.5% to Rs.4,609.49mn -- the largest positive segment driver.

Strategic Investments segment swung from a Rs.(97.17)mn PBT loss to a Rs.646.11mn PBT profit (+Rs.743.28mn), driven by Share of profit of equity-accounted investees nearly doubling to Rs.941.86mn (2025: Rs.540.35mn, +74.3%).
Company (parent) Profit from Operations +71.5% YoY to Rs.1,126.89mn despite only 4.2% revenue growth, driven by Other Operating Income (dividends from subsidiaries) +67.8% YoY to Rs.1,229.92mn.
Group Net Finance Expense widened 15.7% YoY to Rs.1,245.41mn; Group Cash Used in Operating Activities widened to Rs.(2,536.55)mn from Rs.(1,158.10)mn PY.
key_drivers: Tourism sector PBT loss widened by Rs.787.15mn YoY (Rs.(221.77)mn to Rs.(1,008.91)mn) -- the single largest negative driver, unexplained qualitatively in the filing (no MD&A section).
Maritime and Freight Logistics segment PBT improvement of Rs.608.75mn YoY (+58.2%) on 27.5% external revenue growth is the single largest positive driver, more than offsetting the Tourism drag.

Strategic Investments segment turnaround of Rs.743.28mn (from a loss to a profit), driven by equity-accounted investee income nearly doubling, is the second-largest positive driver and pushed Group PBT growth (+74.2%) well ahead of Group revenue (-1.2%).

thesis.thesis_text: Aitken Spence PLC is one of Sri Lanka's largest diversified conglomerates, spanning Tourism (hotels/leisure, including majority-owned AHUN), Maritime and Freight Logistics, Strategic Investments (equity-accounted associate stakes), and Services. In Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), Group PBT grew 74.2% YoY to Rs.1,744,565k and PAT grew 157.7% to Rs.1,044,844k despite essentially flat Group revenue (-1.2%) -- entirely a segment-mix outcome (Note 1.1, p.9): the Maritime and Freight Logistics segment delivered genuine, operationally-driven growth (PBT +58.2% on 27.5% external revenue growth), and the Strategic Investments segment swung to profit largely on rising equity-accounted associate income, together more than offsetting a Rs.787,145k deterioration in the Tourism segment's PBT loss -- a segment that includes SPEN's hotel subsidiary AHUN, itself reporting widening losses this quarter. At ~9.85x annualised P/E and ~0.54x P/B with a steady ~2.84% dividend yield, the stock is statistically cheap, but the filing offers no qualitative explanation (no MD&A section) for the Tourism deterioration, and Group operating cash flow was a net use of Rs.(2,536,553)k this quarter -- a genuinely mixed picture behind the strong headline growth (Interim Financial Statements, source_doc_id 52595, p.2 and Note 1.1 p.9).
